analysis: Examined head lines 610-1755 of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift. Per file_changes (range_map_complete=true), the only changed head range is 3140-3240, which is outside these units. The units therefore show only unchanged test context. That context covers the production gate (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE is default-on, and explicit non-affirmative values disable the cache). It also covers the verified weight-hash binding, test-root isolation behind the ALLOW_EPHEMERAL gate, and the disk budget at half of free space with a 20 GiB fallback. The TTL tests confirm 1800 s as both default and maximum, so the environment can only shorten it, which is consistent with T-041(b). Other unchanged context covers: salt isolation (T-041(d)); corrupt-block deletion with recompute fallback; TTL sliding and sweep; LRU eviction; epoch stability across eviction, TTL and corruption; epoch rotation on binding change; reconciliation that does not follow symlinks; and the write cap. None of this context shows a regression and none of it is new behavior. The changed tests at 3140-3240 are only partly visible in the patch excerpt. They add checks on SSDWholeRootMaintainer header-verdict caching: a header corrupted after an earlier pass, with its mtime restored, must lose its ownership proof (detected via ctime), and a replaced lookalike must be re-read. These tests imply a source change in SSDWholeRootMaintainer that caches per-file ownership verdicts. Integration should confirm the cache key includes ctime, inode and size, so that a same-UID operator (ADV-001) cannot keep a stale ownership verdict. A stale verdict could make TTL/LRU delete a non-owned or replaced file, or skip deleting expired ciphertext (T-041(b)). Source for that maintainer is not in this batch.
